messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The current bug report describes an issue with the core union operation in JXPath where the result nodes are not sorted according to document order. This is clarified by the example XPath expression `string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)` which incorrectly returns "bvalue" instead of the expected "avalue". According to XPath specifications, when a node-set is converted to a string, the string value of the first node in document order should be returned.

The failing test `testUnion()` with the XPath expression `/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]` expects the first contact in document order to be returned. However, the test fails likely because the union implementation does not sort or arrange the combined nodes in document order before returning.

We attempted to inspect the relevant code in the `CoreOperationUnion` class, but found only a simple constructor that takes expression arguments and calls super with them, without further implementation details. Attempts to get the actual `union` operation code led to ambiguous or incomplete results, suggesting the core union logic may be implemented elsewhere, or that the union operation only combines sets without sorting them.

Thus, the root cause is that the union operation in the compiler or runtime does not sort the merged node set by document order before returning, which violates the XPath specification and causes the string conversion to select the wrong node.

The recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated to this issue, so the diagnosis solely depends on the current bug report and test case.

This diagnosis explains why the test fails and the union operation produces incorrectly ordered results. The fix should involve implementing or correcting the node set sorting to document order after union operations.

Next, I will locate the methods that actually perform the union operation, likely under `CoreOperationUnion` or related classes, and examine how nodes are merged and if sorting is done.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
